messages.subject: [gsoc-r] final evals due this week
messages.body_plain:
All,

There are still 15 evaluations due to be completed by mentors.

Students, you might want to check with your mentors and make sure that they have completed your evaluations. All R students have submitted their evaluations, thank you.

Mentors, if your evaluations are incomplete and you have any questions, issues, or concerns, please contact me and Toby immediately. The R organization will be penalized if all evaluations are not filled out, and Google's deadlines are firm. We have a little over three days left to get these done. Expect us to get increasingly more pushy as the deadline gets closer. Thanks for your assistance!

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
http://braverock.com/brian/
Ph: 773-459-4973
IM: bgpbraverock

On Mon, 2017-08-28 at 05:46 -0700, tdh...@gmail.com wrote:

> Dear mentors, please make sure to fill out your final evaluations this week.
>
> Dear students, please edit the Results column of the Table of Coding Projects wiki page https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2017/wiki/table-of-proposed-coding-projects with links
> - to your code (repo or commits on github).
> - to a blog post describing your GSOC project (this is optional but highly recommended). Make sure to include a description of how you heard about GSOC, how you got in touch with your mentors, what were the goals of the project application you submitted to Google before summer, how you met those goals, how did the project evolve/change as summer went on, what you liked, what would you do differently, etc.
>
> For examples of good blog posts, see
> - Rover Van's post from this year http://rovervan.com/post/gsoc/gsoc-summary <http://rovervan.com/post/gsoc/gsoc-summary>
> - Simon Potter's from GSOC2013 https://sjp.co.nz/projects/grimport2/grImport2.html
> - Malith Jayaweera from GSOC2016 http://malithjayaweera.blogspot.ca/2016/08/postcp-change-point-detection-with-gsoc.html
>

messages.subject: Re: [gsoc-r] final evals due this week
messages.body_plain:
Yes, this is expected.

Google will announce the completion of the program to all the students
later today.

At that time, each student will be presented with the 'feedback for
student' section of the evaluation.

Per program rules, you are not allowed to share the evaluation with the
student before Google makes final announcements.

After the Google announcement, I encourage you to have a long talk with
your student about what went well, what could use improvement, and how
the student can keep contributing to the R community after GSoC.

Regards,

Brian
